shonen.text: Manga for teenage boys, with adventure, action, personal growth and friendship.

kodomo.text: Stories for the youngest, with simple messages and colorful art.

shojo.text: Made for girls, with feelings, friendships and personal growth.

seinen.text: Aimed at adults, with more mature and complex stories.

josei.text: For young adult women, with realistic relationships and daily life.

superheroes.text: Heroes with powers and secret identities, from Marvel and DC to auteur comics.

scifi.text: Distant futures, space, technology and dystopian societies.

fantasy.text: Worlds of magic, dreams and fantastic creatures.

noir.text: Investigations, crime, conspiracies and dark moods.
noir.example: V for Vendetta, Batman: Year One

historical.text: Stories about real events or past eras, and the author's autobiographical tales.

series.text: Manga made of many chapters published over time, with a story that unfolds across one or more volumes.
series.example: One Piece, Naruto, Attack on Titan

oneShot.text: Self-contained manga told in a single chapter or volume, ideal for a complete story in little time.

graphicNovel.text: Long, complete stories in a single volume, often by a single author.

omnibus.text: Collections of several issues or volumes in a single edition.

seriesComic.text: Comic series published in issues and then collected in volumes, with a story that continues over time.

action.text: Fights, missions, journeys and goals to reach.

romance.text: Romantic relationships, falling in love and emotional conflict.

fantasy.text: Magic, imaginary worlds and extraordinary creatures.

scifiMecha.text: Advanced technology, robots, the future and technological wars.

horror.text: Fear, tension and supernatural or disturbing elements.

mystery.text: Investigations, secrets and puzzles to solve.

sliceOfLife.text: Everyday life, ordinary relationships and personal growth.

isekai.text: A character is transported to another world.
